newsitem.title: GERMANY: Mercedes denies Werner to move to Deutsche Bahn.
newsitem.headline: Mercedes denies Werner to move to Deutsche Bahn.

text.p: Mercedes-Benz AG on Wednesday denied a magazine report that its chairman Helmut Werner will step down from his post to become chairman of the German railway Deutsche Bahn AG (DB).
In a summary of an article to appear in its next edition, WirtschaftsWoche had reported that Werner had accepted an offer from Daimler-Benz Chairman Juergen Schrempp to leave the company.
"We deny that Werner is going to Deutsche Bahn," a Mercedes-Benz spokesman said. The report, "is taken completely out of the air."
A spokesman for Daimler-Benz said that Werner had not submitted a letter of resignation to the group.
The magazine had reported that current Deutsche Bahn chairman, Heinz Duerr, will step down from his post next year to take over the head of DB's supervisory board, making room for Werner.
The German media has been rife with speculation in recent weeks that Werner will leave his post as part of a massive restructuring of Daimler being pushed ahead by Schrempp.
According to the Daimler chairman's plan, Mercedes and other Daimler units will be brought closer within the corporate structure and be made less independent.
Werner, whose unit is responsible for the bulk of Daimler's sales, has opposed the plans and reportedly has threatened to resign if his concerns are not addressed.
